text: So I booked this hotel for my family's last night in Morocco before leaving the next day to return to America after visiting my husband and I in Taza. So my standards aren't very high when it comes to hotels etc as I have slept and ate in some crappy places. This hotel on the surface appears very nice. motels the reason the bed frame goes all the way to the floor is to make the room easier to clean - so maids don't have to kneel down and search under beds to see if the last occupant had left a empty water bottle and perfume bottle under the bed. In this case in this hotel - the beds are on these plastic and wooden slatted platforms with a lot of empty space for trash to collect - if maids aren't diligent if they are lazy and don't want to pick up the trash under the bed. I also noticed as did my mother that it was HOT in the rooms. We tried to turn on the thermostat in both rooms So then my mother called the front desk asking them how to work the thermostat because it didn't seem to be working - As the Ibis Hotel Chain which is owned by Accor Hotels states 15 minutes to fix problems - it was on the flyer in the room. They sent a guy up to her room - he looked at the thermostat - then asked if they speak French - no we are Americans and its their first trip to Africa - no they don't speak French and then leaves. A few minutes later the front desk calls and says that "At this time of year the thermostat is not turned on Well this is weird and frustrating to me and my family considering all the materials throughout this hotel's media and advertisment is talking about how it wants you to have the best night's sleep possible. Why even put individual thermostats in the rooms if your not going to let the guests use them? I can't sleep when its hot in my bedroom - neither can my husband It was Hammam hot hot and humid - in both our rooms and we couldn't turn the AC on at all! We went downstairs and tried to go to the restuarant - which in the elevator is advertised to be open until 11pm - we arrived at 10:30pm and were turned away - told quite curtly by a waitress they were closed - they told us go to the bar and order from the other menu there. So we ordered at bar in which we were told only two entree's on the menu were avalible quiche and chicken panini. I personally think its pretty shameful such a large chain hotel ran out of 24 entrees listed on the menu - I wondered if the Ibis hotels have a supply chain issue when it comes to food items - which given there is one everyone else in my family ordered the chicken panini - which turned out to be a complete joke - there was no chicken in fact it was SO lacking chicken that my mother said - I guess this is a mayo panini hold the chicken. The hotel also had this strange perfume throughout all the common areas such as halls bars and reception that I ended up sneezing at every time I left our room. Back to the thermostat issues - so we had thought that our hot rooms would be solved by opening the windows - which did reduce the temperature My husband is such a light sleeper that each time one buzzed near his ear - he woke up. The noise pollution from outside our hotel with the window open would have kept me up We got breakfast down stairs - which was the only high light of the stay besides the parking for our rented car and the shower in my mother's room. I wouldn't recommend staying here to anyone else after our stay and from a PCV that is saying something especially at this price point in Morocco

The route from the airport is through a scruffy Quartier Industriele the hotel is a pleasant relief. it is an attractive hotel with secluded gardens and a good pool. The railway staion doesn't intrude as it has about 8 services a day and means there are taxis and shops beside the hotel. The public areas are decorated in traditional Morrocan style and the rooms are good sized and clean. Breakfast was good in the pleasant restaurant when we used it in the evening it was good value and competent the food was dull (an achievement with a Morrocan brochette!) the receptionist was very helpful and gave good advice receipt and you got the impression this was a direct transaction between the receptionist and the company. The Hotel was a gentle 15 minute stroll through the Ville Nouvelle to the Medina and the Gueliz had a very continental athmosphere with good cafes and hassle free shopping in the "Prix Fixe" shops - a lot easier than the hustle and hype of shopping in the souks. this one has the advantage of being in walking distance of the Medina and the facilities of the New Town and closer to the airport.
label: positive

text: This is the hotel for someone who is doing Marrakech on the cheap It's not really close to downtown so that is one reason the room prices are less. You pay about 45 euros for a room with breakfast. They have junior suites for 70 euros and senior suites for 90 euros. The room I had was immaculate the large bed was comfortable and the flat LCD TV was nice and doesn't take up too much space. Not much of a view (mine was of the swimming pool). Very limited menu at the restaurant food was nicely prepared and tasty. I ordered a sandwich and fruit after 2300 from the reception and it was delivered promptly and was well prepared and presented and very reasonable price. Stay here if you are looking for clean and inexpensive and you don't mind not being too close to the center of town.
label: positive

text: All I can say about this hotel is: "EXCELLENT STAFF" starting from the bellman to the front desk. I contacted a person their called Alamy who was VERY cordial and of an excellent attitude. The hotel is very convenient in being very near to the train station. The politeness of the staff is of a special taste that made my stay a memorable one.
label: positive

text: The main point that the room was NOT clean including the bed. I'm 100 sure that the bed linen was not changed a lot of hair on the sheets pillows looked dirty. The toilette was not too clean as well. it was already around midnight and we were not sure if other rooms are better. Nice points: very tasty breakfast (e.g. pancakes were excellent) garden with a pool. On the way back we stayed 4 nights in 100 times nicer place, Anyway, I would not say that Ibis price is a good value. Otherwise, service was OK. Note concerning the previous review: Petit taxi should not cost more 15 drh inside the city (usually less 80 -100 Drh is fine to go from the city to the airport. Not sure about appropriate price to go from the airport to the city. I paid 150 Drh,
label: negative

text: This Ibis hotel is situated right next to the railway station We requested a room overlooking the garden and pool and not the often busy Av Mohammed V that passes the other side of the building. Our room was the shower was good - nice strong flow of hot water. Breakfasts were served in the hotel restaurant from very early in the morning to midday There was a very nice breakfast spread each morning with fresh pain aux raisins and croissants fruit etc.. You can catch a bus to Djamma El Fna from right outside the hotel - A petit taxi from the railway station forecourt to the medina should cost you no more than 50 dirhams. The hotel is of course well-placed for both rail travel and the adjacent Supratours bus station which operates to Agadir watch out as it seemed to us that many Moroccans were on the look out for extra bucks and that included certain hotel workers we met. Its proximity to the railway station was not a problem as Marrakech is the end of the line and there isn't really such a thing as Crosby Stills Nash's "Marrakech Express"!
label: positive

text: This hotel is a little oasis in the centre of such madness!! The rooms are typical of Ibis. generally clean and comfortable. The breakfast here was very good and the evening meals are OK a little pricey compared to the city. The staff are quite friendly compared with others we came across in Morocco. The pool area and the garden and bar really make this place as they give it a relaxing atmosphere and something to do in the very hot days in Marrakech. The only negative is the music in the garden every night until 11pm which makes it impossible to sleep as it is very painful. Overall this hotel is fine for long weekend
label: neutral

text: The pool area is lovely and the breakfast buffet was very varied and generous The location is ok The food served isn't culinary genius I was unwell one day and eating in the hotel made things a lot easier and was actually a very nice experience. You can also have a drink outside by the pool which is lovely.
label: positive

text: The rooms are rather small and in need of refurbishment. Having said that I would recommend this hotel. The hotel is clean and well run. The gardens and pool are excellent. The food is generally good and the breakfast excellent. The hotel is conveniently located with a bus to the medina every few minutes. It is next to the railway station and 10 minutes from the airport. The staff are friendly and helpful. The hotel is very good value for money. Plus: This is a very good value hotel has a nice pool and fair size garden for the price. The breakfast is buffet. Rooms at the back are fairly quiet. Minus: The rooms smell of smoke. The room itself isn't as clean as other Ibis in Europe The breakfast pastries aren't the freshest. It's right next to the station.
label: positive

text: Hotel was more rooms a bit on the small side you dont spend much time in your room and it was clean and comfortable clean towels every day which is important to us! Breakfast was ok the danish pastries are delicious! Too cold to sit by the pool for long the hotel puts the garden in the shade by mid afternoon at this time of year so only had a half hour out there. Pleasant little restaurant across the road (sold alcohol!!) The Marrakech Tour bus was a good way of getting the general feel of the place. we definately did the right thing and enjoyed our three nights in Marrakech!
label: neutral

text: Staff were friendly and the hotel has a nice looking pool ( it was too cold for us to use it). Rooms were very run down The air conditioning was also not working and the room was very hot. This was not such a bad thing as it was winter and cold outside we were far too warm and our friends who were staying in the same hotel had the opposite problem - really cold rooms with the heating not working. Breakfast was standard a selection of croissants (not great looking ones) yoghurt and some bread. Shower was quite good tho and the hotel bar was ok. we walked everywhere and there are a few restaurants and bars which are not very far from the hotel. The hotel also arranged a day trip to Essouira for us. fantastic sea food and great beach.
label: neutral

text: Not the best hotel. We decided to stay here because it was near the train station (literally next door) and we were arriving late into Marrakech chain hotel. Ordinary, functional, somewhere to sleep The hotel is fairly dated with salmon-coloured walls in the bedroom cracked tiles in the shower old blankets on the bed stained carpets etc. it was relatively clean so for the price we couldnt complain. The staff werent the friendliest, Location-wise, it suits if you want to be near the train station for an early train , its not that near the medina you will need to get a taxi walk quite far to get to the main square. it was a bed for the night if its a good standard of comfort youre after
label: neutral

text: It was really lovely directly in the hotel. The guide was billingual -Eng French-'what was really useful as my girlfriend is French!!!. The meals offered were copious and delicious. Overall prices really convenient. by checking in there you grant yourself an efficent service at a good rate.
label: positive

text: in what can only be described as an over-rated expensive city The state of the room we were offered when we arrived was quite frankly a health hazzard. The amount of damp in the room from the shower was causing the plaster to bubble up and black mold to appear. The carpets we also very stained and Overall if you have experienced Ibis in Europe When we complained they did move us to one of the renovated rooms on the first floor This sums up our experience of being a tourist in Marrakech; robbed! I cannot recommend this hotel
label: negative

text: Noisy rooms need the air cond. you could not open a window because of the noise and the bedspread was too hot for the weather in question. Unfriendly staff. Breakfast like a fastfood restaurant with a tray The room seemed to be clean the floor was not very hygienic. The shower was nice flooded the floor in the bathroom. There were only one towel by person the same towel to facehands and body.
label: negative

text: We stayed in this hotel for almost 2 weeks and really enjoyed it.Decent clean rooms .Don't expect anything else than the standard Ibis-room shower (no bath) clean towels every day.We had a renovated room so no stained carpets proper and clean. this hotel is situated almost on the train station of Marrakesh we did not experience too much noise at all.The pool area was lovely dusty city.Breakfast is a buffet not so standard as the European Ibis-breakfast.Bread Danish pastries excursions can be booked at the reception. Staf was friendly and helpfull.
label: positive

text: On arrival at the hotel my wife and I found the room to be a bit smaller than we were used to and overlooking the train station there was some noise. On awakening we noticed that the air conditioner was not REALLY working (making noise not cooling). He again offered and said "It is a bigger room" Sure enough we were upgraded to a suite very roomy and nice The staff were all very helpful from the desk staff to the room attendants I would reccommend this hotel, would reccommend the suite. As for the street noise our suite was very near the main door and seemed well sound-proofed so really what little noise there was was not noticed. outstanding value pay (alot more) for them elsewhere.
label: positive

text: Yes this is an Ibis hotel so expect standard service standard accomodation. The rooms on the 1st floor have been renovated therefore cleaner and with LCD screen. Dont bother with the other floors small dark rooms way out dated. I advise you to have breakfast outside the hotel there are many places across the road a 2 min walk to the station will satisfy most. Having checked the breakfast at the hotel They have a swimming pool it was rather cold when I was there Ideal location right next to main train station 10 min walk to Gueliz area and other main areas. I was charged for breakfast Stay there if your looking for budget hotel close to centre
label: neutral

text: Stayed here for one night en-route from the west coast to Menara Airport. Room was OK - a bit run down I noticed that they were in the middle of a renovation so perhaps things are better now. Petit Dejuner (breakfast) was just that - little! Breadconserves and coffee... Great location for the train station and right next to the Supratours bus station if you're heading to AgadirEssouria etc.
label: neutral

text: We were a family of 4 staying in 2 double rooms. The hotel is well priced and spotlessly clean. The pool is lovely and the gardens very atmospheric with fruit trees and a lovely patio. The hotel is well situated next to the Railway Station and is well serviced by Taxis (make sure you agree a price before getting in). The bar is also quite good, The staff are very friendly and there is on-site security as well. The restaurant is excellent It certainly doesn't 'rip you off' like most hotels in the Uk has a wide span of opening times for breakfast lunch dinner. There is a wide selection of good food drinks. Breakfast is buffet continental style. well priced restaurants within a few minutes walk past the Station take care with the traffic. The hotel is well presented, there was some painting re-carpeting going on on the 2nd floor during our stay The rooms are also spotless and quite spacious, one of our rooms had a bit of flaking paint and some missing mosaic tiles in the bathroom (big deal !) The rooms were changed daily and the maids even went to the trouble of folding the children's nightwear not usually expected in a 2-star hotel ! There was the occassional noise from the Station (train hooters), Overall, we enjoyed our stay and we would definitely stay there again...... Bon voyage !
label: positive

text: We were scheduled to arrive in Marrakech by train late in the evening and planned to depart early the next morning by rental car. as our train from Casablanca was 1.5 hours late and we were quite happy that it took less than 5 minutes to walk from the station to the hotel. renovated room on the third floor: as the hotel was fully booked that evening The room was typical Ibis-style and relatively clean, Beds were in good shape and the breakfast buffet was better than expected. Overall the hotel was okay for a short stay especially given the relatively low price
label: neutral

text: We had a great stay. The room was quite nice right next to the train station We just got the bus from the airport and once the driver (who was really helpful) worked out we were right next to the train station it was a very cheap transport to the hotel. Hotel was really nice The staff were helpful and the hotel was a walking distance from the centre of town
label: positive

text: Was looking to book a hotel for one night away from the crazyness of Marrakech as had to leave early the next day and this ended up being perfect for a number of reasons: 1. Its just around the corner from the superb new train station 2. Its also on the road to the airport 3. Its a 10 minute (30 dirham) taxi ride from the main square 4. Its Ibis so expect the usual good value for money quality and extras such as free wifi bar restaurant 24-7 etc.... All in all given the circumstance you could do a lot worse that staying here if you are not looking for a Riad experience
label: positive

text: The Ibis Marrakech Centre Gare is right next to the train station and the Supra tours bus stop. Its very easy to reach the medina by cab (20 dirhams) and the new railway station next door has some great restaurants. The airport is 15 mins away. The room was newly renovated and was clean and comfortable Breakfast was average Overall i would recommend this if you want to stay away from the busy medina and in a clean standard budget room. Please make sure to visit the spa at Riad Mehdi (les bains de marrakech) - its the best. If you get tired of the tajines and couscous try Bombay lounge and restaurant for indian food and Muraille D'Asie for chinese and sushi.
label: positive

text: Ibis Place de La Gare is just besides the great new Marrakech train station with shops fast foods (Mc). Agadir by car. Plenty of restaurantsbars nearby. Breakfast a the hotel is good with nice views of the garden. Rooms are ok
label: positive

text: and spent a couple of days just lounging around the hotel. It has great areas around the pool and gardens as well as indoors near the bar. Comfortable pool chairs comfortable indoor chairs. Surprisingly quiet considering it's right beside the railway station and our room overlooked the tracks! The pool area is great The railway station has some great restaurants as well as McDonalds and KFC The restaurant at the hotel doesn't open till 7.30 at night and the menu is pretty ordinary. Breakfast is okay. Nice bread. taxis are waiting at the door and quite cheap. Helpfulness of reception staff varied (for us)with their ability to speak English,
label: neutral

text: This hotel may seem out of the way omelet breakfast shops fish restaurants a butcher which has a tagine over in the floor and some fold down tables in the back smallish room The rooms were clean we had our bed made up everyday The staff were friendly preferring to visit our local bakery and have coffee omelet served in a hot pan eaten with bread - the shop was so busy we waited on the street for a table The pool was nice We ate from the bar menu one night after a late arrival back from Esouaira and the chicken panini with chips did the job a little over priced Its also a great location for getting the train to your next destination Ok, not the most luxurious of hotels, We did have a problem on the first night because our room (309) was overlooking the very busy main road. Now that was not the problem as we are in a busy city, the window did not shut properly and the aircon was extremely noisy and the room also had a strange smell to it. That was no trouble at all and we were moved to room 304 opposite which was much better. This room overlooked the pool and was more peaceful, it was opposite the station The aircon was also quieter and the window shut! We only had breakfast a couple of mornings which was very good - typical continental breakfast We ate there one evening from the set menu which we found excellent. a nice bottle of red with our meal went down well. haggle and you may get it cheaper! a lovely clean hotel with a pool which was much needed in the 36c heat and very helpful and excellent staff.
label: positive

text: The hotel is all you want from a budget hotel Rooms are nice and Clean I had view on the Station and the swimming pool, nice. Breakfast could be better Staff are really nice. you'll get your value for money there. If you want to eat in a Local restaurant try the Restaurant de la Paix right behind the Imperial hotel Excellent value for money delicious Tagine great Mixed grill
label: positive

text: i returned to hotel. a very good hotel ...............food was excellent
label: positive

text: I asked for a triple room was given a squashed double with no fridge and balcony. Room also stank of cigarettes. Glad we spent our holiday in Agadir as Marrakech was a huge let down.

text: This Ibis is located right next to the train and bus stations in Marrakech and as such is great as a transport hub, less great as a place to sleep. The room itself was in ok condition A small cockroach in the shower hinting at the lack of renovation. the bed and sheets were fine so no complaints there. Service was not great as the staff seemed arrogant. We had dinner (admittedly quite late - 930pm) and the steak was pretty limp and tasteless... We stayed at an Ibis in Casablanca which was orders of magnitude better so I would still recommend Ibis

text: We arrived around 9pm and the receptionist tried to speak as much as possible in English. the room was ok. As we were only staying one night a bed breakfast and the pool would be enough. We went down for a meal and the waiter was not the nicest person in the world the meal was delicious! The bed was comfy and we slept really well. The breakfast was really nice with NOT an English offer (I'm not a big fan of English breakfast). The pool served its purpose very well. The staff was a bit not into customer service

text: The Ibis Marrakech Centre Gare hotel is just besides the great new Marrakech train station with shops fast foods (McDonalds The room we stayed was comfortable . there are a lot of cafés on the other side of the street. The room was very quiet and it was clean. The staff was very helpful! you take the bus (line 14 66) which stops in front of the hotel on the other side of the street and ends at the Jamaa el Fna market place.

text: Stayed here for two nights one at the beginning and one at the end of our trip to Morocco. The airport bus leaves you right outside the train station and local buses take you to the djemaa el fna square and souks in around 10 mins. Rooms were typical of an Ibis hotel - 2 single beds pushed together a place to put a suitcase Hotel also had a pool which was great to cool down after the heat of the souks. Staff were friendly and helpful.
label: positive

text: It's easy to get here on the airport bus 30 dirhams round trip and the hotel is right behind the train station. Free wifi in the lobby not the rooms. at least it was easy to get buses to Djemaa El Fna right outside the hotel. Don't bother with the breakfast Rooms are small There is a cheap place to eat called Restaurant Comedie about 3 blocks towards the medina. the staff are nice
label: neutral

If you're looking for a comfortable clean and reasonably priced hotel that is well situated in Marrakech Thank you to everyone for making our stay so enjoyable.

text: This hotel is fine. It's a convenient location close to the train station and right next door to Supratours so perfect for a day beforeafter a visit to elsewhere in Morocco. as the hotel layout doesn't allow you to truly relax as it's not a lesuire hotel ( having a great pool!) due to it's location and situation in the city. We also stayed at the Ibis in Essauoria a new hotel and it was excellent - would highly recommend. is an older hotel and in need of a bit of an update. Essauoria itself is a great place very chilled out with a great beach and some great restaurants - check out the reviews. I would stay at this hotel again, I'd be in search of a cheap deal to make it more worthwhile. Several buses take you into the medina from right outside the hotel. If you want to go to Oasisira water park it's only a short walk to catch the free bus there. Also, it's close to the new part of town where most of the best restaurants and more upmarket shops are located. cheaper and more comfortable than a grande taxi.

text: Typical Ibis hotel. Large rooms and clean. The staff is kind and efficient. It's a little noisy it is very close to the center of the city. Rooms were fine. being next door to the station. staying several nights you might want to consider something closer to the rest of the city for us it was great.

text: clean places near people and places we are interested in. at the Ibis near the Railway station. We were met by attentive manager who took great interest in making sure our stay was memorable. made onward reservations to other hotels and enquired daily about our experiences.

text: This hotel is ideally located to manage travels in out of Marrakesh. The night after I needed to print an on-line ticket and even if it was very late the receptionist kindly helped with it. The room was clean and the bed comfortable. good value for money.

text: The hotel gardenpool is a real oasis in an otherwise hot dusty and busy city.This is an older still comfortable conveniently placed hotel The plunge pool is over 3 metres deep and a welcome relief from the 43c we experienced one afternoon( ask for a room overlooking the pool as itll be quieter than the street side.The trains stop running at night and we were aware of the railway announcements during the day the train noise was not a issue) The hotel is conveniently situated next door to the railway station and Supratours bus terminal.There is a free internet terminal downstairs for clients use.The staff are very obliging .There are hairdryers to borrow at the desk.During Ramadam some restaurants were closed for the month opening hours were altered.There are still the KFCs and Macdonalds if that is your choosing.It takes about 30 minutes to walk to the Dnenna el Fna.There is an Acima supermarket along Ave Mohammed Abdelkrim el-Khattabi north from the roundabout near the Railway Station.The number 19 airport bus stops by the railway station and picks up for return trip on the Ave Mohammed V opposite the Theatre down from the kiosk.The cost of a return ticket of 30 dirhams be aware of the petit taxis who will stop anyway wanting your business.All in all a well placed no frills Hotel and very attentative staff.
label: neutral

text: The hotel was clean and very good value for money (i booked this online The location of this hotel is right next to the main train station in Marrakech On the other side of the wall of the hotels garden are train tracks and platforms. One train comes around every 30mins (that I noticed whilst I was there) so the noise wasn't even loud. just to give a sense of location. Location wise - amazing. for a budget hotel your located IN This is basically the modern side of Marrakech as opposed to "Old Town" which is the old-skool side (it's surrounded by walls and is where the main square New Town's centre is probably around 10 minute walk turning left out the doors of Ibis amazing bustling restaurants and public gardens. As for the hotel itself the service was friendly and courteous. It goes Arabic (conversational) French (official) they will do their very best to speak English back to you. The hotel manager speaks very good english and is very friendly. The hotel waiters will usually attend to you within minutes of sitting down even if you don't want anything and just want to use the free Wi-fi. The bar food is satisfying if you want a snack For a budget hotel Room was cleaned every day. Seen some bad reviews: just remember it's a budget hotel! If you plan to spend a lot of your time in a hotel
label: positive

text: It is approximately 25 minute walk to the famous medina square. Yes, it has competitive prices, 50 a night for 2 guests is stil not enough to keep us from booking this Ibis again. We could hear the tv of the room next door and also the flushing toilet of the room upstairs. It does have a nice garden where guests may enjoy their breakfasts (which was good). This place is of "motel" quality, if you are really looking for a cheap price and fairly clean location It is a matter of standards. Id like to note that they have limited parking space and as it is common with the Ibis chain of hotels in Morocco expect to have limited toiletries and cheap-thin quality towels (they only provide you with 2 towels daily per room because of the hotel policy). if you shower at night expect to use the same damp towel next morning. if you ask for 2 more towels even if there are two guests in the room because is their policy.

One of the waiters (head waiter?) On our last night it seemed that the regular waiting staff were (there were only two) both off All in all okay for a two night stay I guess any longer and you'd be best to upgrade to a better hotel. The hotel seems to be a travellers inn rather than a base for a weeks holiday.

If you are arriving by train this hotel is perfectly located. It is also not far from the airport. It is a bit away from the tourist attractions I use the regular hop on hop off tour bus as a form of public transport when in Morocco - your can get on and off for two days at most of the important places - and there is a stop not far from the hotel. A taxi might be better value for a group It is a modern hotel and many visitors prefer to stay in more traditional riads, the rooms are good the service is mostly good access to transport is good and it has the extra amenity of a garden and pool. There are also a number of nearby restaurants and cafés. The hotel needs to look at his attitude. The service quality makes this hotel so fantastic! Thanks to Amine who always offers outstanding service at the bar and at the restaurant and welcomes guests with a genuine smile! And to Yassim - at reception - for his patience and helpful suggestions. Room for improvement? The breakfast could have more options I'm aware that most hotels don't turn the AC "on" during the Moroccan winter foreigners still find it hot and stuffy

text: Ouarzazate is easily reached by sharedindividual taxi by bus in an average journey time of 4 hours from Marrakech. up a hill and opposite the Kasbah Taourirt and immediately next to the Ibis (which looks lovely with a huge pool and big screen outside). The reception staff were very welcoming and we were very pleased with our room which contained a fridge and a safe. All rooms also have air con and satellite tv. They are advertised as having a balcony these are shared with your neighbour and also have no chairs All the public areas are very nice with a lovely pool area which never really seemed to get busy (towels provided at reception). The bar area is huge and has very reasonably priced drinks and snacks. Breakfast is served downstairs in the main restaurant and is very nice with a huge selection of food hot drinks and juices. We also ate dinner in the restaurant on our first night and had a very enjoyable meal. Many local people try and entice you in via any number of entrances. Note that there is an official entrance which is opposite the artisanal shopping complex which takes you into the Kasbah that has recently been restored (10dh). Ouarzazate town (which is much more modern than I was expecting) has quite a few shops a decent supermarket (bizarrely enough selling more alcohol and pork than anything else!) and a number of restaurants. I read somewhere that Chez Dimitri has changed its name to Café Mogador it hasnt! The 2 restaurants are miles apart! 2 fillet steaks 2 desserts water and coffee all for about 40 and it was the best steak wed eaten in a long time!!!! It was so good we ate there 2 nights is a row! The reception staff are very helpful and provided us with maps and organised an onward taxi to take us to Zagora. All in all the hotel made a lovely change to all the riads that wed been staying in and I would definitely recommend it - worthy of its 4 stars definitely!
label: positive
